data.long_meaning: In Late Latin, Terese means 'to reharvest' or 'to gather in'. This name was popularized in the Middle Ages by Saint Teresa of Avila, a Spanish mystic and reformer of the Carmelite Order, who is known for her writings on prayer and contemplation. The name Terese carries the meaning “Reharvest, to gather in” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Terese usually hope their child will grow to embody reharvest, to gather in and live with faith, good character and purpose.
